name: dispatch_contention
supersedes: protocol.json (version 1, decision B on both devices, nothing installed)
mechanisms: resource.fma_smsp / instruction.service issue_interval_cycles of the fma_smsp classes (candidate P)
question: Version 1 (r2, both devices) left the FP32 pipe model open: a single warp's independent FFMA stream issues 1 / cycle per SMSP (ilp8, and the installed service_latency thr of 1.045 / 1.007), yet dependent FFMA chains of W warps interleaved on one SMSP cost 4 / 5 / 6 / 8 cycles per step for W = 1..4 (both devices, identical), i.e. 2 cycles per warp-instruction once several warps share the SMSP -- while FMNMX / IMAD chains follow their installed 2-cycle (16-lane) units exactly. Independently, ffma2_operands (b300-r2b1) measured a single warp's FFMA stream with three distinct, non-reused register sources at 1.49 cycles per instruction (installed 1.007 comes from a reuse-friendly form), and register_operands r1 could not key that on a static per-instruction fact because ptxas mixed `.reuse` flags inside the windows. The two observations point at the same unresolved mechanism: what limits an SMSP's FP32 issue rate when the operands are not served by the operand reuse cache -- the FP32 pipe itself (candidate P) or register-file operand reads (candidate O)? Round 32 / 35 attribution needs the answer: fa3 softmax (3 consumer warps per SMSP, FMNMX / FFMA / MUFU streams: hardware 2.5x the engine's time, stall reason dispatch 15 %) and BL3-F32 (SIMT FP32 GEMM, 0.876) are FFMA-dense multi-warp code.

engine_rules_declared_before_data.baseline: the present engine: one issue per cycle per SMSP (scheduler.policy.issue_slots 1, cursor_commit, try_next_on_block); per-class unit occupancy issue_interval_cycles on the class resource (fma_smsp 1.045 / 1.007 for FFMA, fmaheavy_smsp 2.0 for IMAD, xu_smsp 8.26 / 8.0 for MUFU), fractional accumulation; dependent issue at max(producer issue + result_latency_cycles, previous issue + control-word stall); yield_hint = 1 - raw control bit 4 moves the SMSP cursor to the next warp.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.P (pipe pairing): resource fma_smsp has two copies, each with initiation interval 2.0 for every class bound to it (the installed ~1 values are the paired rate); copy 1 admits an instruction only when the SMSP's immediately preceding issue was the same warp's immediately preceding instruction (program order). A single warp's back-to-back stream therefore alternates copies at 1 / cycle; instructions of different warps interleaved on the SMSP take copy 0 at 2 cycles each. Operand form plays no role.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.O (operand read): a per-SMSP operand collector: every issued instruction reads its distinct general-purpose source registers from a banked register file, bank(r) = r mod NB, one read per bank per cycle; an operand is NOT read when it is served by the reuse cache, i.e. the same warp's immediately preceding instruction (program order) carried the reuse flag on that operand slot with the same register AND that instruction was the SMSP's immediately preceding issue (an intervening issue from another warp loses the cached operands -- r2's dependent chains, whose a / b operands carry .reuse on every instruction, cost 2 per instruction as soon as warps interleave, which a per-warp cache that survives interleaving cannot produce; that alternative is therefore not a candidate). cost = max over banks of the number of reads in that bank (0 for instructions without register-file reads: immediates, constant-bank, uniform and RZ operands do not count; a register named twice counts once; 64-bit pairs count both registers). Two collector forms: 'x' (exclusive): the SMSP issues nothing else until issue + cost; 'p' (per bank): each bank is busy for its own read count and an instruction issues only when every bank it reads is free. NB in {2, 4}. Candidates: O2x, O4x, O2p, O4p. The class units stay as installed (so IMAD / FMNMX keep their 2-cycle units; the collector only adds a floor).
engine_rules_declared_before_data.not candidates: a class-independent dispatch interval (version-1 candidate A: refuted by ilp8 at 1 / cycle); a +1 forwarding penalty when the producer is not the SMSP's last issue (would also raise IMAD / FMNMX W = 2 chains to 5, r2 measured 4.00 / 4.00); a reuse cache that survives an intervening warp (above).

probe: tools/microbench/dispatch_contention/probe/contention_v2.cu (new file; v1 probe untouched). One CTA of 4*W warps, W in {1, 2, 3, 4} (warp w on SMSP w % 4), bar.sync before every repetition (v1 addendum), every warp's lane 0 records BOTH clock64 reads (t_s, t_w) so the host derives the per-warp window T_w = t_w - t_s and the CTA window T_cta = max_w t_w - min_w t_s over the active warps of the repetition. Window = U units, U in {64, 128, 256}, fully unrolled, inline asm volatile so ptxas neither folds nor reorders; operands that must be registers are bound with register constraints. Variants (all f32 FFMA unless stated; a, b, a_j, b_j are kernel arguments copied to registers before t_s; d / d_j are the chain accumulators): dep3r `fma d, d, a, b` (v1 ffma: 3 distinct registers, a / b reusable); dep3n `fma d, d, a[i%4], b[i%4]` (ring of 4 pairs: 3 distinct registers, never reusable); dep2 `fma d, d, a, d` (2 distinct registers, a reusable); dep1 `fma d, d, 0f3F800001, d` (1 register, immediate multiplier); ilp8 `fma d_j, d_j, a, b` j = i % 8 (v1: 8 independent chains, a / b reusable); ilp8n `fma d_j, d_j, a_j, b_j` (8 chains, 16 distinct constant registers: 3 reads, never reusable); ilp8n2 `fma d_j, d_j, a_j, d_j` (2 reads, never reusable); ilp2 `fma d_j, d_j, a, b` j = i % 2; imad `mad.lo.u32 d, d, ia, ib` (v1 control: 2-cycle unit); mixed (v1: fma / max.NaN alternating on d); mufu.<op> dependent chains with op in {ex2, rcp, rsqrt, lg2, sin, tanh} (approx.ftz.f32; tanh approx.f32), W = 1 only, record cells. --launches 16 --reps 65, two runs (run-a, run-b) per device.
sass_gate: tools/microbench/dispatch_contention/sass_check_v2.py: per kernel the window between the repetition's two SR_CLOCKLO reads holds exactly U instructions of the variant's class (mixed U/2 + U/2; mufu.<op>: U MUFU.<OP>; a mufu op that ptxas expands to more than one instruction fails the gate and is unrealised); the chain dependence is real where the variant is a chain. For every window instruction the gate records opcode, destination, source operands (register numbers, immediates / constants / RZ flagged, `.reuse` suffix per operand), and the control word (stall, raw yield, reuse bits, scoreboards); the recorded `.reuse` suffixes must agree with the control-word reuse bits (bit s = source slot s), else the kernel fails the gate. The instruction list of the U = 256 kernel is the replica's program; U = 64 / 128 lists must be prefixes of it in opcode / operand form (checked).

derivation.T(variant, W, U): per-warp: median over warps x launches x reps (first rep dropped) of t_w - t_s; CTA: median over launches x reps of max_w t_w - min_w t_s
derivation.slope: OLS slope of T over U (cycles per instruction), separately for per-warp and CTA windows, per run; cell slope = mean of run-a / run-b
derivation.replica: tools/microbench/dispatch_contention/model_v2.py simulates one SMSP holding W copies of the gate's instruction list (the two CS2R reads included as ordinary 1-cycle instructions with their control words) under each candidate rule, with the device tree's installed result_latency_cycles / issue_interval_cycles / resource per class (configs/trees/<dev>.json, instruction.service), the engine's scheduler (one issue per cycle; cursor stays on the last issued warp unless its instruction's yield_hint = 1 - raw bit 4 is 1, then advances; scan from the cursor, first ready warp issues; a warp is ready when its sources are ready, previous issue + stall has passed, and the rule's resources admit it), all W warps released at cycle 0. Predicted per-warp T = issue(CS2R t_w) - issue(CS2R t_s) per warp (median over warps), predicted CTA T = max - min over warps; predicted slopes by the same OLS over U. For the mufu cells the replica uses the installed MUFU result latency, so a mismatch there measures the leaf, not the rule (record only).
derivation.error(rule, cell): |predicted slope - measured slope| for the per-warp slope and for the CTA slope; a cell passes a rule when both are <= max(5 % of the measured slope, 0.25 cycles per instruction)

decision.usable cell: OLS residual <= 2 % and run-a / run-b slope agreement <= 3 % (or <= 1 cycle per window) and the kernel passes the SASS gate; unusable cells are listed and do not gate
decision.gating cells: dep3r / dep3n / dep2 / dep1 / mixed at W in {1, 3, 4}; ilp8 / ilp8n / ilp8n2 / ilp2 / imad at W in {1, 2, 3, 4}. The W = 2 dependent FP32 cells (dep3r / dep3n / dep2 / dep1 / mixed at W = 2) are reported and not gating: r2 measured the dependent FFMA chain at W = 2 as 5.00 per step on both devices while IMAD / FMNMX at W = 2 are 4.00, a one-cycle effect confined to exactly two interleaved FP32 chains that none of the declared candidates represents; it is bounded (<= 1 cycle per dependent FP32 instruction at 2 warps per SMSP) and left as a recorded residual. mufu.<op> cells never gate.
decision.rule: per device: a candidate is accepted when every usable gating cell passes it; the installed rule is the first accepted candidate in the declared order. If 'baseline' is accepted nothing changes. If no candidate is accepted nothing is installed, the per-cell table (measured vs each candidate) is reported and the protocol is marked unrealised for that device; a version 3 must declare new candidates before measuring again.
decision.evidence: measured when the accepted candidate's maximum error over gating cells is <= 5 % of the measured slope on both runs individually; experimental when it needs the 0.25-cycle absolute allowance on any cell or the two runs disagree by 3-5 % on any gating cell
decision.both devices: each device decides on its own data; the engine carries both rule families behind leaves so the devices may differ (P on one, O on the other, or different NB)

install.P: configs/mechanism_tree/common/resources.json: fma_smsp copy_count 2 and a new per-resource attribute `second_copy_pairs_with_previous_issue` = 1 (the engine admits copies >= 1 only when the SMSP's last issue was this warp's previous instruction); <arch>/leaves/instruction.service.json: issue_interval_cycles of every class bound to fma_smsp with installed value < 1.5 -> 2.0, source dispatch_contention.<device>.v2r<n>; CTest fixture: one warp 8 independent FFMA -> 1 / cycle; two warps' dependent chains -> 2 cycles per instruction.
install.O: new common mechanism register_file.operand_read (event initialization, scope smsp) with fields enabled (0 / 1), banks (NB), collector (0 exclusive / 1 per bank), reads_per_bank_per_cycle (1, structural); <arch>/leaves with the accepted NB / collector, source dispatch_contention.<device>.v2r<n>. Converter (python and cpp segment builders identical, py == cpp gate): REGS rows gain per-source flags `reuse_served` (the static predecessor in program order carries the reuse flag on this slot with the same register) and `pair` (64-bit source: class table of 64-bit register-pair sources plus `.64`-suffixed names); segment / container format version bump, formats.md. Engine: at issue, cost from the REGS flags and the leaf (reuse_served counts only when the SMSP's last issue was this warp's previous instance), collector occupancy checked in resource_ready and committed with the issue; journal / wait bucket resource. CTest fixtures: single warp 3-read no-reuse stream (1.5 at NB 4 with spread banks / 2.0 at NB 2); two warps' 3-read chains interleaved -> 2 per instruction; reuse-served stream -> 1 / cycle.
install.after install: tree build && tree validate --strict (five classes 0); py == cpp on the 5 standard cases when the converter changes; one two-architecture 500 A/B round against the current baseline (hp $A/merge/rba, bw $A/merge/if36; facts $A/merge/cbk), report table row, status, docs/en/microbench.md

record_only.mufu ops: per op the W = 1 chain slope (= dependent latency of that MUFU op); h100 r2 showed MUFU.EX2 17.07 against the installed MUFU result 23. Installing a per-op MUFU latency needs a class split (MUFU.EX2 / RCP / RSQ / LG2 / SIN / TANH) in the converter routing tables and the service leaf -- a separate service_latency addendum, not this protocol.
record_only.W = 2 dependent FP32 chains: reported next to the candidate predictions

not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no change of candidates, order, thresholds, gating set or variants after data; the yield bit and the control-word stall counts are facts of the program (round 30 stall floor) and are not modelled here.

addenda.written_before: any v2 GPU run (dry run of model_v2.py on the v1 h100-r2 SASS / samples only)
addenda.text: (replica detail) The installed FFMA / FADD / FMUL issue_interval_cycles are 1.045 (h100) / 1.007 (b300): the service_latency thr harness's rounding of a 1 / cycle rate (v1 ilp8 measured exactly 1.00 on both devices). In the replica a fractional interval just above 1 opens a one-cycle hole every ~22 instructions in which the scheduler switches to another warp, which turns the greedy single-warp window into an interleaved one and inflates the per-warp window of the other warps by a whole window length -- a qualitative effect of a 4.5 % leaf residual, not of any candidate rule. The replica therefore treats class issue intervals <= 1.1 as exactly 1.0 (all candidates alike; P sets the fma_smsp copies to 2.0 regardless). Also recorded from the dry run: the v1 U = 64 and U = 256 kernels allocate different registers (dep3r: R2,R4,R5 vs R10,R2,R3), so the bank cost of a cell can differ between its U kernels; the replica simulates every U kernel's own program (sass_check_v2.py records all three), and the prefix check (opcode / operand kind / reuse pattern) is recorded as prefix_ok, not gating.

addenda.written_before: any v2 GPU run (same dry run of model_v2.py on the v1 h100-r2 kernels: dep3r / imad / mixed / ilp8 / mufu.ex2 remapped to the v2 names)
addenda.text: (gating set) mixed at W = 3 / 4 moves from gating to record only. Dry run against the r2 measurements (mixed 5.00 / 5.00 / 5.00 / 6.00 for W = 1..4): the replica under O2x predicts 5.51 / 7.35 at W = 3 / 4, under P 5.01 / 5.01. For O2x a 12-cycle steady-state schedule of the four warps' FFMA(2) + FMNMX(1) pairs exists (F0 M5 / F3 M8 / F6 M11 / F9 M2 with the 5-cycle cross-pipe stalls satisfied) and equals the measured 6.00, but the engine-policy replica (cursor commit, first ready warp from the cursor) settles into a bunched pattern (FFMA FFMA FFMA, FMNMX FMNMX FMNMX with one-cycle holes behind the 2-cycle alu unit) at 14.7 per pair; a pure round-robin cursor gives the same 7.35 and breaks ilp8. The multi-class mixed cell therefore measures the hardware scheduler's packing on top of the rule, which no declared candidate (all share the engine's scheduler) represents; its W = 3 / 4 cells are reported next to the candidate predictions. The single-class windows (dep* / ilp* / imad) have no packing freedom and remain the gating set. Other replica fixes from the dry run: unsupported placeholder nodes (MUFU.EX2 on h100) fall through to the root class leaf; the two CS2R reads use L = 1 / no unit as declared (the h100 CS2R.CLOCK leaf's 6-cycle alu interval would otherwise stagger the warps' starts by 6 cycles).

addenda.written_before: version 3; after reading v2r1 (h100-v2r1 / b300-v2r1, model_v2.py)
addenda.text: (reading of v2r1; decision: no candidate accepted on either device, nothing installed; protocol v2 unrealised) Probe outcome: ptxas placed every kernel-argument constant the chain does not redefine in UNIFORM registers (dep3n ring: `FFMA R10, R9, UR8, R2`; dep2: `FFMA R5, R5, UR5, R5`; ilp8n2: `FFMA R13, R13, UR8, R13`; mixed FMNMX `R6, UR10`), ilp8n re-loaded its 16 constants with LDC.64 inside the window (gate fail, unusable), the opaque moves did not pin them, and v2's dep3r / mixed FFMA / imad lost the .reuse flags v1 had (`FFMA R12, R12, R2, R3`). So the forms actually measured, by general-purpose register reads, are: dep3r 3 / ilp2 3 (reuse flags on alternate instructions) / ilp8 3 (served) / imad 3 / mixed FFMA 3 / dep3n 2 / dep2 1 / dep1 1 / ilp8n2 1. Measured per-warp slopes (both devices identical to 0.02): dep3r 4 / 5 / 6 / 8; dep3n, dep2, dep1 4 / 4 / 4 / 4; ilp2 2 / 3 / 4.3 / 6; ilp8 1 (h100 all W; b300 W = 2, 3 unusable per-warp -- greedy windows bimodal -- CTA 2.0 / 3.0 / 4.0); ilp8n2 1.0; imad 4 / 4 / 6 / 7.85; mixed 5 / 5 / 5 / 6; mufu W = 1: h100 ex2 / rsqrt / lg2 / tanh all 17.0 (installed MUFU 23 from the r3r rcp+add pair), b300 ex2 13.95 (installed MUFU.EX2 14), rsqrt / lg2 / tanh 17.95 (installed MUFU 24); mufu.rcp window empty (ptxas folds rcp(rcp(x)) even from asm volatile -- PTX is PTX), mufu.sin = FMUL.RZ + MUFU.SIN (expected). Reading: every form with three general-purpose register reads not served by the reuse cache costs 2 issue cycles of its SMSP when warps interleave (dep3r 2W; ilp2 pair = 2 + 1 = 3 cycles -> 3 / 4.5 / 6 per instruction at W = 2 / 3 / 4, with W = 1 latency-bound at 2; mixed FFMA 2 + FMNMX 1 = 12 cycles per 4-warp round = 6), every form with one or two register reads costs 1 (dep3n / dep2 / dep1 / ilp8n2 flat at the latency bound), and the served form ilp8 issues 1 / cycle: an operand-read limit of two general-purpose register reads per SMSP per cycle, integer (3 reads = 2 cycles, not 1.5: dep3r W = 4 is 8.00). None of the declared candidates has that shape: P charges every fma_smsp instruction (dep2 / dep1 predicted 6 / 8, measured 4 / 4); O2x / O4x charge by bank conflicts (dep3r's R12 / R2 / R3 happen to collide under both, but h100's U = 64 kernel R2 / R6 / R7 does not under mod 4 and still measures 8; O4x predicted 2.9 - 3.4 from the kernel mix); the per-bank forms let a second warp slip in on ilp8 (1.5 - 2.5 predicted, 1.0 measured). dep3r W = 2 = 5.00 (record cell) remains unexplained by any rule here (ilp2 W = 2 = 3.00 fits exactly). Version 3 declares the operand-port candidate before measuring again, with the constants made non-uniform so that the dep3n / dep2 / dep1 / ilp8n / ilp8n2 forms read general-purpose registers as intended.
